summary: The cycle 1 patch plan (F1-F4) has been correctly applied. The _retry_request helper mirrors BaseUploadPipeline._retry_request with retries on 500/502/503/504 and exponential backoff; Instagram and TikTok collectors are wrapped. The unused reason parameter is removed from _unavailable_snapshot. The Instagram token lookup calls load_auth_config() first then reads from the environment. Retry-on-500 tests exercise the shared backoff helper. All gates pass (372 tests, OK). No new issues found.

decisions.decision: Guide left open: how to handle the quality/spec_audits/analytics_capabilities.md reference in the Twitter unavailable reason. The guide's Twitter collector emits an unavailable reason referencing quality/spec_audits/analytics_capabilities.md, but that file does not exist in the repository. I chose to keep the reference as-is in the reason string because the guide explicitly specifies this text and the file is referenced as a research artifact that may be created separately.
decisions.why: The guide explicitly specifies the Twitter unavailable reason text including the reference. The file does not exist yet, but the reference is user-facing documentation pointing to research that established the metering wall. Keeping the guide-specified text is correct.

decisions.decision: Guide left open: how to stamp correlation fields (duration_seconds, title, configuration_hash) when artifact records may not have them. The guide says 'Nulls, not errors, when missing.' I chose to look up the artifact record by artifact_id from the attempt and read duration_seconds and title from it, falling back to None when the artifact or field is absent. The configuration_hash comes from the attempt record's own configuration_hash field, which is always present on published attempts.
decisions.why: The guide says 'Nulls, not errors, when missing.' The implementer correctly looks up the artifact record and falls back to None when fields are absent. The configuration_hash comes from the attempt record's own field, which is always present on published attempts.

decisions.decision: Guide left open: whether the collect_platform_metrics function should be called with a timeout. The guide says 'bounded' but does not specify a timeout value. I chose a 120-second timeout on the future result, which is generous enough for platform API calls while preventing indefinite hangs. The dedicated executor is short-lived and shut down after each pull.
decisions.why: The guide says 'bounded' but does not specify a timeout value. A 120-second timeout is a reasonable choice that prevents indefinite hangs while being generous enough for platform API calls.
